papers.title: Generating Shared Latent Variables for Robots to Imitate Human Movements and Understand their Physical Limitations
papers.abstract: Assistive robotics and particularly robot coaches may be very helpful for rehabilitation healthcare. In this context, we propose a method based on Gaussian Process Latent Variable Model (GP-LVM) to transfer knowledge between a physiotherapist, a robot coach and a patient. Our model is able to map visual human body features to robot data in order to facilitate the robot learning and imitation. In addition , we propose to extend the model to adapt robots' understanding to patient's physical limitations during the assessment of rehabilitation exercises. Experimental evaluation demonstrates promising results for both robot imitation and model adaptation according to the patients' limitations.

summary_en.motivation: To enable assistive robots to imitate human movements and adapt to patients' physical limitations during rehabilitation.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian Process Latent Variable Model (GP-LVM) is used to map visual human body features to robot data for imitation and adaptation.
summary_en.result: Experimental results show promising performance in robot imitation and model adaptation to patient limitations.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through robot imitation tasks and adaptation to simulated patient limitations.

papers.title: Numerical approximation of elliptic problems with log-normal random coefficients
papers.abstract: In this work, we consider a non-standard preconditioning strategy for the numerical approximation of the classical elliptic equations with log-normal random coefficients. In \cite{Wan_model}, a Wick-type elliptic model was proposed by modeling the random flux through the Wick product. Due to the lower-triangular structure of the uncertainty propagator, this model can be approximated efficiently using the Wiener chaos expansion in the probability space. Such a Wick-type model provides, in general, a second-order approximation of the classical one in terms of the standard deviation of the underlying Gaussian process. Furthermore, when the correlation length of the underlying Gaussian process goes to infinity, the Wick-type model yields the same solution as the classical one. These observations imply that the Wick-type elliptic equation can provide an effective preconditioner for the classical random elliptic equation under appropriate conditions. We use the Wick-type elliptic model to accelerate the Monte Carlo method and the stochastic Galerkin finite element method. Numerical results are presented and discussed.

summary_zh.method: 利用Wick型椭圆模型作为预条件子加速蒙特卡洛和随机伽辽金方法
summary_zh.result: Wick型模型在特定条件下可有效加速经典随机椭圆问题的求解
summary_zh.validation: 数值算例验证预条件子的加速效果

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently approximate elliptic PDEs with log-normal random coefficients by reducing computational cost.
summary_en.method: A Wick-type elliptic model is used as a preconditioner to accelerate Monte Carlo and stochastic Galerkin finite element methods.
summary_en.result: The Wick-type preconditioner provides significant speedup under appropriate conditions, especially for large correlation lengths.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on benchmark elliptic problems demonstrate the acceleration performance.
